learning_outcomes.text: Adequate knowledge of mathematics, science and related engineering discipline-specific subjects; Ability to use theoretical and applied knowledge in these fields in complex engineering problems
Ability to design experiments, conduct experiments, collect data, analyze and interpret results for the study of complex engineering problems or discipline-specific research issues.
Ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary teams
Ability to communicate effectively verbally and in writing
Awareness of the necessity of lifelong learning; the ability to access information, follow developments in science and technology and constantly renew oneself
Knowledge of standards used in engineering practices
Information about the effects of engineering practices on health, environment and security at universal and social dimensions and the problems of the age reflected in the field of engineering

syllabus_topics: General information in the first meeting, laboratory safety and some explanations on laboratory workings
Quantitative systematic analysis of group I cations, their separations and recognition of their reactions

Quantitative systematic analysis of group III cations, their separations and recognition of their reactions
Quantitative systematic analysis of group IV and V cations, their separations and recognition of their reactions
Quantitative systematic analysis of General cations, their separations and recognition of their reactions
Acid-base neutralization titration (Determination of acetic acid in the vinegar)
Precipitation Titrations (Chloride determination by Volhard method)
Complexymetric titration with EDTA (determination of hardness of water)
Redox titration (Oxalate and Ca determination with KMnO4)
